title: docker: writable docker-socket-proxy exposed unauthenticated on LAN (wud-proxy)
description: docker/dockerhost/wud-proxy-dh/docker-compose.yaml:6-12 and diskstation/wud-proxy-ds/...:6-12 run docker-socket-proxy with POST=1 (write), socket mounted RW (not :ro), published 0.0.0.0:2376, no auth. Any LAN host gets full Docker control = host root. WUD only needs read + digest. Fix: POST=0, :ro socket, bind 127.0.0.1 or internal net.

title: docker: Redis exposed on 0.0.0.0:6379 with no password
description: raspberrypi5/redis/docker-compose.yaml:5-6 has no requirepass and binds 0.0.0.0. Backs traefik-kop cross-host routing state; any LAN host can read/write. Bind internal/localhost and set a password.

title: ansible: tailscale authkey leaks into logs (missing no_log)
description: ansible/roles/openclaw/tasks/main.yml:288-295 runs 'tailscale up --authkey=...' without no_log:true, so the key is rendered into stdout/CI logs. The exit_node_nordvpn role (tasks/main.yml:227) does this correctly. Add no_log: true.

title: docker: Home Assistant runs privileged + network_mode host
description: raspberrypi5/homeassistant/docker-compose.yaml:5,11 uses privileged:true + network_mode:host. HA compromise = full Pi compromise. Replace privileged with specific device mounts (Zigbee/BT) if that's the need.

title: docker: GitHub self-hosted runners mount docker.sock RW; dh/rp non-ephemeral
description: docker/{dockerhost,diskstation,raspberrypi5}/github-runner-*/docker-compose.yaml bind /var/run/docker.sock RW. Any workflow (or PR build if enabled) escalates to host root; only diskstation is EPHEMERAL, dh/rp persist state between jobs. Keep repo-scoped, never enable untrusted PR triggers, make all ephemeral, and use a socket-proxy or rootless.

title: Homelab security & hardening review (2026-07)
description: Findings from a full multi-subsystem review (Docker/Ansible/OpenTofu/k8s/secrets) of the homelab repo, July 2026. No secrets are leaked (all SOPS/age ciphertext verified); the gaps are runtime hardening (Docker socket exposure, privileged containers) and operational resilience. Theme: the right patterns (socket-proxy, gluetun kill-switch, SOPS) already exist but are applied inconsistently, plus a few unsafe defaults.

title: ci: gitleaks configured but never enforced
description: .gitleaks.toml exists but no pre-commit hook, no CI workflow, no git hook runs it — so it catches nothing. Wire it into a pre-commit hook or a runner CI job.

title: secrets: single age recipient = single point of failure
description: .sops.yaml uses ONE age recipient (age1vamq...) for all rules; losing that key makes every secret unrecoverable, no backup. Add an offline backup recipient to all creation_rules and run 'sops updatekeys' on each encrypted file.

title: ansible: installer scripts executed without checksum verification
description: openclaw/tasks/main.yml:91-116 (+ Tailscale/NodeSource) download and run installers; the 'verify checksum' step only debug-logs the hash, nothing asserts it. Pin+verify sha256 before executing.

title: ansible: host_key_checking disabled globally
description: ansible/ansible.cfg:4 sets host_key_checking=False for all hosts; MITM risk during LAN provisioning (before Tailscale). Prefer known_hosts management.

title: tofu: Proxmox TLS verification disabled by default
description: tofu/proxmox/*/variables.tf:18-22 default proxmox_insecure=true (used by provider.tf:13); API token sent over unverified TLS to pve.home.alborworld.com. Default to false.

title: tofu: encrypt state client-side (Garage state holds live S3 creds)
description: tofu/*/backend.tf use S3/Garage backend with no client-side encryption; the garage stack persists garage_key.tofu.secret_access_key in plaintext tfstate. Anyone with read on the tofu-state bucket gets live S3 creds. Add encrypt=true/SSE or rely on verified Garage-side encryption.

title: docker: unauthenticated admin endpoints reachable on LAN
description: portainer-agent 9001 (no TLS/auth) and Garage S3 Admin API 0.0.0.0:3903 (diskstation/garage:8) are LAN-reachable. Restrict to internal networks / Tailscale.

title: docker: add no-new-privileges:true across stacks
description: Zero of the 76 compose files set security_opt: no-new-privileges:true. Cheap systemic hardening, esp. for internet-adjacent and socket-touching services.

title: docker: apply the socket-proxy pattern consistently (raw RW sockets)
description: You already run dockerproxy-* (read-only). But: traefik-kop-dh:7/-ds:7 mount the raw RW socket; raspberrypi5/wud:32 uses raw RW socket (dh/ds route via wud-proxy); dockerproxy-dh:11/-ds:11 bind 0.0.0.0 while dockerproxy-rp:11 correctly uses 127.0.0.1. Route all through the read-only proxy on localhost.

Need to: 1) Test if container-level rules work without cluster firewall enabled 2) If not, enable cluster-level firewall via pvesh/API 3) Consider managing this in Tofu. Risk: enabling cluster firewall could affect all VMs/LXCs on nuc13 if they don't have their own firewall configs.
close_reason: Verified: Proxmox per-container firewall (202.fw enable:1) IS enforced without cluster-level firewall. Test: flushed in-container iptables, port 853 still blocked by Proxmox layer, port 80 still allowed. Cluster-level firewall is optional — per-container enable flag is sufficient. No action needed.

title: Fix systemctl --user bus error in OpenClaw LXC
description: OpenClaw gateway fails to start with: 'Gateway service check failed: Error: systemctl --user unavailable: Failed to connect to bus: No medium found'. This is because the openclaw service runs as a system service (not user), but OpenClaw internally tries to use systemctl --user which requires a D-Bus user session. Need to either enable lingering for the openclaw user (loginctl enable-linger) or configure XDG_RUNTIME_DIR so the user bus is available inside the LXC.
close_reason: Fixed by adding XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS to systemd service template (resolved via Ansible getent), plus loginctl enable-linger

title: Add audio transcription with Whisper to OpenClaw
description:
Add voice message transcription using faster-whisper so OpenClaw can process audio/ogg messages.

Steps:
1. Install faster-whisper runtime in a Python venv on the OpenClaw LXC (VMID 202), plus ffmpeg
2. Create ~/bin/transcribe_ogg.py script using WhisperModel('base', device='cpu', compute_type='int8')
3. Hook into OpenClaw inbound message flow: detect audio/ogg media, run transcription, replace message text
4. Quality tuning: vad_filter=True, consider model size (base→small→medium), set language for speed
5. Optional: enable TTS responses for full voice loop

Key details:
- Use faster-whisper (CPU, int8) as the runtime — easiest for LXC without GPU
- Script takes an audio file path, outputs transcribed text to stdout
- Integration point is the inbound message handler/middleware — add conditional for audio/* mimeType
- Model 'base' for speed, upgrade to 'small'/'medium' for accuracy later

title: Investigate Proxmox firewall rules for OpenClaw LXC via Tofu
description: Check if the bpg/proxmox Tofu provider supports defining firewall rules at the container level. If so, codify rules equivalent to the current iptables setup (default DROP inbound except from Proxmox host, restrict outbound to 80/443) in the OpenClaw Tofu stack. Proxmox-level firewall is stronger than in-container iptables since it can't be bypassed if the container is compromised.
notes: bpg/proxmox provider (v0.70+) fully supports container-level firewall via two resources: proxmox_virtual_environment_firewall_options (default policy DROP/ACCEPT per container) and proxmox_virtual_environment_firewall_rules (specific inbound/outbound rules with ports, protocols, source IPs). Rules enforced at hypervisor level — can't be bypassed from inside LXC. No firewall config exists in the stack yet. Implementation: add both resources to tofu/proxmox/openclaw/main.tf targeting container_id=202 on nuc13. Need to account for Tailscale UDP, DNS, and Ollama connectivity.
close_reason: Proxmox hypervisor-level firewall applied via Tofu. Default DROP inbound/outbound with allowlists for SSH (LAN), Tailscale WireGuard/STUN, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS. Verified Tailscale connectivity post-apply.

title: Add dedicated VLAN for OpenClaw LXC
description: OpenClaw LXC (VMID 202) sits on the default vmbr0 bridge with no VLAN isolation. Per merox.dev deployment guide, it should have a dedicated VLAN in Proxmox for network segmentation. However, the existing iptables rules (default DROP) + Tailscale mesh already provide strong isolation. The practical security gain of adding a VLAN is minimal for a homelab — revisit if untrusted devices join the LAN or if the threat model changes. Would require: new VLAN on router, Proxmox bridge VLAN tag in Tofu, static IP on new subnet, firewall rule updates.
notes: 2026-02-23: Assessed as low priority. Existing iptables (default DROP) + Tailscale provide equivalent isolation. VLAN adds marginal security for a homelab but introduces router/provisioning complexity. Static DHCP reservation set on router for LXC IP. Deprioritized to P4 — revisit if untrusted devices join the LAN or for learning exercise.
